items.title: First Thing: Cop31 talks collapse without deal in blow to planet’s future climate
items.summary: More than two weeks of talks in Turkey fail to produce a resolution to tackle climate crisis. Plus, a savage review of Melania’s new documentaryGood morning. The world’s nations have failed to reach agreement at the Cop31 talks in Turkey. In a dramatic conclusion to the summit, major powers rejected what they called an unacceptable deal on the future of the climate, which failed even to mention fossil fuels. The proposed deal “failed to meet the moment”, said Ireland’s environment minister, Darragh O’Brien.What was in the proposed agreement? The Antalya pact invited nations to electrify their economies, called on wealthy countries to fund climate adaptation for poorer ones, and urged signatories to minimise any “overshoot” of the Paris agreement’s 1.5C global heating threshold. However, it failed to endorse the “transition away from fossil fuels” demanded by more than 130 countries, instead including controversial provisions on carbon capture and storage technology that critics argued would perpetuate fossil fuel use.What precipitated the collapse of the talks? In this analysis piece, the Guardian’s environment editor, who was at Cop, explains that after a marathon negotiating session ran more than 40 hours past its deadline, a small group led by Saudi Arabia refused to accept any mention of a “transition away from fossil fuels”. While such holdouts would normally force through a watered-down compromise, nearly 40 nations – led by the EU, the UK, small islands and least developed countries – broke with precedent and openly rejected the weakened text, refusing to salvage the usual face-saving semblance of unity.What is the latest in the Ukraine war? Rescuers raced on Monday to find residents trapped under the rubble of a block of flats that partly collapsed in a Russian strike, after overnight attacks on the Kyiv region killed at least 14 people. A strike on Dymer, about 45km north of the capital, hit a five-storey building, killing at least 11.What has happened to a Russian ship docked in Libya? A Russian warship in Benghazi was struck in the early hours of Sunday in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel. The strike severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette that had stopped to refuel and take on supplies. Continue reading...

items.title: Monday briefing: What could Andy Burnham’s reset mean for the UK?
items.summary: In today’s newsletter: The prime minister has reopened the debate over a future relationship with a changed EU – as the bloc faces the rise of the far right, a protectionist economic agenda and growing defence ambitionsGood morning. Nobody really wants to think about Brexit any more, save for the original Brexiters, who seem delighted that Andy Burnham’s “reset” with the EU has given them an excuse to get the old gang back together. But arguments about whether the UK should rejoin the EU will reignite in parliament this week, as Burnham briefs MPs on the deal he agreed on Friday.That deal wasn’t so much a victory as the culmination of Keir Starmer’s incrementalist approach to UK-EU relations. Its core agreements haven’t been ratified by member states yet, and the EU won’t sign them off until Britain resolves a dispute over tuition fees for European students. Burnham is apparently “determined” to take the UK back into the EU, but don’t expect any progress on that before the next general election.Cop31 | The EU, the UK and allies in the developing world rejected what they called an unacceptable deal that “failed to meet the moment” in a dramatic finish to the UN talks in Turkey. The proposed deal failed to endorse a away from fossil fuels that more than 130 countries demanded.Russia | A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel.Weapons| The Red Cross and other rights groups have warned that it will soon be too late to properly regulate the development of autonomous weapons. The warning came as the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons concluded without an agreement on an instrument for regulating autonomous weapons.UK news | Dozens of hospitals are so short of money they may not be able to continue caring for patients and are being forced to make “unpalatable” cuts to services and staff, the Guardian can reveal.West Bank | Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot condemned arson attacks by militant Israeli settlers on Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank after dozens of settlers raided Palestinian communities overnight on Saturday.Monday | FIFA is set to announce that the UK will host the 2035 Women’s World Cup.Thursday | RMT will begin a series of eight 24-hour strikes on the London Underground over the next three months due to a dispute over a four-day week for its drivers.Sunday | Spain will hold snap parliamentary elections in what will be the country’s sixth general election in 11 years. items.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
items.summary: Leeds offer Chelsea a lesson, Newcastle’s summer recruits struggle and Jules Ahoka makes a name for himselfWhat to make of Manchester United’s utterly torrid start under Mauricio Pochettino? To go glass half full as the new head coach had only three days to prepare the side for the trip to Anfield, the hope will be that time will cast the 4-0 humbling from Liverpool as the falsest of false starts. The glass-half-empty scenario, though, is that here was an XI packed with internationals that had zero clue how to sort out a dire beginning themselves. Leny Yoro’s very early red card may have been questionable but for the wall to evaporate and allow Dominik Szoboszlai’s subsequent free-kick to arrow home was damning evidence of how immature Pochettino’s new charges are. From here it became a debacle and the players, if they have anything about them, need to apologise to the head coach, hold a meeting between themselves and demand they start taking responsibility. The Welshman had not won a major televised event since 2022 and may have thought it might not happen again after losing three finals this year alone.But with Luke Littler and Luke Humphries exiting early, Price took his chance with a brilliant 16-11 win over Gian van Veen in Wolverhampton. Price claimed Grand Slam glory for the fourth time, but this one will surely mean the most to him. Continue reading...

items.title: Alcaraz puts Zverev in shade as world’s best beats No 1 for first ATP Finals title
items.summary: Spaniard wins final 6-2, 7-6 (7) against new world No 1Alcaraz the fourth to win career grand slam and ATP FinalsThe titles of ATP world No 1 and the best male tennis player in the world are carried by two different names. This has always been clear throughout this messy, injury-ravaged men’s season but it was underlined in the grand finale as Carlos Alcaraz ended his campaign with a statement victory, defeating the top-ranked player, Alexander Zverev, 6-2, 7-6 (7) to win the ATP Finals for the first time.So much of Alcaraz’s fortunes this season were defined by the wrist injury that forced him out for four and a half months during the spring and summer. No matter, he still managed to tick the two most important items off his to-do list this year. Continue reading...

items.title: Jensen Huang’s reported affair was ‘most expensive sex since Helen of Troy’, US senator says
items.summary: John Kennedy looks to Trump leaders as he asks how China evidently bypassed export controls for Nvidia’s top AI chipsInvoking Greek mythology, US senator John Kennedy has characterized former Nvidia chief executive officer Jensen Huang’s reported affair with a suspected Chinese spy as “the most expensive sex since Helen of Troy”.The Louisiana Republican’s allusion to the legendary figure whose desirability was such that it caused the mythic Trojan war came during an interview on NBC’s Meet the Press on Sunday. Host Kristen Welker asked Kennedy, known for his colloquialisms, if US national security was put at risk by Huang’s affair, given the position his company’s chips have occupied at the forefront of the artificial intelligence boom. Continue reading...

items.title: I covered myself in sleep trackers to find the very best
items.summary: Get a better night’s sleep with monitoring and guidance from smartwatches, smart rings, smart bands and sleep earbudsThe best sleep masks and best Bluetooth sleep masksGetting quality sleep is just as crucial as getting enough sleep. And how you feel in the morning only tells part of the story. Smartwatches, smart bands, smart rings and sleep earbuds can all help fill in the details: how long it took you to doze off, how long you spent in deep sleep, how restless you were, your resting heart rate, even if you have night-time breathing difficulties.Armed with this information, you can learn how your lifestyle affects your sleep. Maybe your after dinner cappuccino triggers a night of tossing and turning, or you’re more restful after evening workouts. As the wise GI Joe once said, knowing is half the battle. And the more you know about your sleep, the better chance you have of improving it. Continue reading...

items.title: McBurnie’s added-time double snatches win for Hull to shock 10-man Brighton
items.summary: Amid the talk of Brighton being surprise title contenders this season, these are perhaps the afternoons which show the margin that still exists, and how the Premier League can provide the most punishing of wake-up calls at any moment.Make no mistake about it, Fabian Hürzeler’s side will play far worse than this over the next few months and win. They are still second in the table. How they left Hull without even a point almost defies belief given the dominance they enjoyed for large parts of the contest. But for all the statement victories and the headline-grabbing moments, these games are the ones which can trip you up the most. Continue reading...

items.title: ESPN mourns ‘one of the best human beings ever’ after NFL analyst Tom Jackson dies at 75
items.summary: Former player known for partnership with Chris BermanJackson was member of Broncos for 14 seasonsESPN is mourning “one of the most influential and beloved figures” in the broadcaster’s history after the death of Tom Jackson at the age of 75.Jackson played for the Denver Broncos for 14 seasons at linebacker, and was a two-time All-Pro selection, before turning to broadcasting after his playing career ended in 1986. He was a key part of ESPN’s NFL coverage, most notably alongside Chris Berman, for 29 years before his retirement in 2016. Continue reading...
